description: Hi! I'm MARIAM, solo team member for the "Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts" challenge. Building an interactive dashboard using Python, Bolt, and Framer to track how astronauts' health risks compound during long missions. Open to teammates interested in data analysis, UI design, or space biology—curiosity matters more than experience!
summary: BIO TRACK is an AI-assisted astronaut mental well-being monitoring prototype designed for long-duration space missions. It brings together physiological indicators, sleep and activity patterns, and cognitive task performance from ASTRO MIND in one interactive dashboard. An experimental Random Forest model estimates stress patterns using electrodermal activity (EDA) features from the QoL_Stress research dataset. The platform also summarizes sleep and activity indicators from the MMASH dataset. By combining complementary signals, BIO TRACK aims to help users notice patterns that may deserve attention and support human review. The prototype uses Earth-based human research data, not live astronaut data, and is not a medical diagnostic tool.
details:
BIO TRACK is an interactive web-based prototype designed to explore astronaut mental well-being during long-duration space missions.

The platform includes seven main sections: Overview, Health Monitoring, ASTRO MIND, AI Analysis, Recommendations, Mission History, and About.

Health Monitoring summarizes sleep, activity, and heart-rate indicators using the MMASH dataset, which contains data from 22 healthy participants. Sleep records were available for 21 participants.

For stress estimation, we developed an experimental Random Forest model using electrodermal activity (EDA) features from the QoL_Stress dataset. The model was evaluated using five-fold participant-independent GroupKFold validation, achieving a mean accuracy of 65.00% and a mean macro F1-score of 64.55%.

ASTRO MIND is an interactive cognitive task game. Users can import a game report into the dashboard to review task accuracy and response time.

The frontend was built with React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS. The prediction service uses Python, FastAPI, and scikit-learn.

BIO TRACK's creative approach is to combine physiological, sleep, activity, and cognitive indicators into one well-being picture rather than interpreting each signal in isolation.

The current prototype uses Earth-based human research datasets and illustrative interface examples. It has not been validated with astronauts, clinically validated, or endorsed by NASA. Its outputs are intended for research exploration and human review, not medical diagnosis.
